status: Working proposal; mandatory new-patient intake confirmed under U1/D-25

pages.title: One connected care journey.
pages.subtitle: YSCC can connect assessment, participation and follow-up, then build towards a wider learning system.
pages.label: THE PRODUCT IN ONE MINUTE

blocks.text: Make it clear what is needed, who contributes, what has happened and who acts next.

items.title: Care delivery
items.body: Collect and review useful person-level information.

items.title: Service improvement
items.body: Resolve quality issues and turn evidence into action.

items.title: System evidence
items.body: Use governed outputs for oversight and research.

blocks.note: The wider learning cycle is an ambition: findings must return to services, not stop at reporting.

items.title: Understand and contribute
items.body: Eligible person and family tasks, clear visibility, suitable support and reliable confirmation.

items.title: Know the next action
items.body: The right episode, interpretable evidence, outstanding work and accountable handover.

blocks.title: What this is not
blocks.body: Not an autonomous clinical decision-maker, an assumed EMR replacement or an unrestricted participant portal. Wider care and reporting capabilities still need scope approval.

decision.title: LEADERSHIP TAKEAWAY
decision.text: Align on the care-collection foundation and approve wider capabilities separately. The proposal is ready for review, not production authorisation.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 01, sections 1-6. S1/S2 and CMDCS persona draft (CP1).

pages.title: Choose the launch boundary.
pages.subtitle: Keep reported capabilities, proposed delivery scope and broader ambitions visibly separate.
pages.label: SCOPE AND EXECUTIVE DECISIONS

items.title: A complete collection loop
items.body: Mandatory intake for every new patient, then assessment and repeat measures; eligible collection; permissions, correction, queues and owned referral follow-through.

items.title: Four explicit scope choices
items.body: Satisfaction surveys, service logging, detailed discharge content and historical migration/export. Decide included, later or excluded for each.

items.title: The broader CMDCS ambition
items.body: Ongoing care records, personal progress, centre dashboards, implementation learning, governed reporting, exchange and research. Phase and access remain open.

blocks.title: Resolve the MVP / Stage 2 conflict
blocks.body: Oli's captured Slack message reports direct person/family collection in MVP. The persona PDF places direct self-report in Stage 2 and a person dashboard in MVP. Neither conflict is resolved by this executive edition. D-21.

rows: Confirm core assessment and clinical rules
Caroline + clinical/content leads
Approve permission, access and retention policy
Clinical + legal/privacy + data governance
Choose scope, phases and named delivery owners
Product + programme leadership

decision.title: ASK AT THE NEXT REVIEW
decision.text: Resolve D-21, choose the D-15 scope items, and name accountable owners for the production decisions. Do not convert a persona ambition into a launch promise.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 01, sections 5-8; U1/D-25 confirms intake; D-26/D-27 remain open.

pages.title: Value starts at the point of care.
pages.subtitle: A simpler contribution process is valuable only when it remains understandable, appropriate and trustworthy.
pages.label: CUSTOMER JOBS TO PRODUCT VALUE

items.name: Kai / person
items.job: Share how I am doing and understand the next step.
items.pain: Repetition, unclear visibility and uncertainty about receipt.
items.response: Eligible self-report, plain explanations, support and confirmed submission.
items.gain: A clearer, more manageable contribution to care.

items.name: Deb / family carer
items.job: Provide useful context and understand how to help.
items.pain: Feeling excluded or overloaded; unclear role boundaries.
items.response: A separate appropriate task, clear visibility and distinct authority checks.
items.gain: Involvement without assuming access to another person's answers.

items.name: Jess / treating clinician
items.job: Collect, interpret and act on the right information.
items.pain: Duplicate entry, fragmented context and ambiguous status.
items.response: An episode-centred plan, eligible channels and separate review/handover actions.
items.gain: Less avoidable coordination effort and clearer clinical context.

blocks.title: Scope distinction
blocks.body: Kai's personal dashboard and Jess's full ongoing-care record are candidate capabilities. The current assessment/collection baseline does not deliver them by implication.

decision.title: TEST THE VALUE
decision.text: Can people explain purpose and visibility, complete an appropriate task, and understand what happened? Can staff identify what remains? Completion rate alone is not proof of fit.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 02, canvases A-C; CP1 pp. 4-6; CR-01/CR-02 and D-21.

pages.title: Turn reliable data into useful action.
pages.subtitle: Different evidence users need different products. A single dashboard is not the value proposition for everyone.
pages.label: SERVICE AND SYSTEM VALUE

items.name: Rachel, Tom and Ananya
items.job: Run the service and maintain reliable, comparable records.
items.pain: Manual follow-up, unclear definitions and fragmented reporting.
items.response: Owned quality work, verified-source correction and, if adopted, governed metrics and releases.
items.gain: More interpretable operations and accountable resolution.

items.name: Sam / implementation scientist
items.job: Understand fidelity and help centres improve.
items.pain: Data without local context; findings that do not reach practice.
items.response: Candidate implementation views linked to centre context and improvement actions.
items.gain: Evidence that leads to practical support and follow-up.

items.name: Priya, David, Maya and Helen
items.job: Commission, oversee, exchange or research for approved purposes.
items.pain: Inconsistent data, weak comparisons and unclear access processes.
items.response: Candidate governed reports, exchange contracts and study-specific request/release pathways.
items.gain: Defensible interpretation and controlled use, not unrestricted care access.

blocks.title: Evidence discipline
blocks.body: These pains and gains are hypotheses. No verified savings, clinical impact, missing-data baseline or research-turnaround improvement has been established.

decision.title: INVESTMENT QUESTION
decision.text: Which user decision will each data product improve, and how will we test that? Require an owner, a defined output and an approval boundary before adding scope.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 02, canvases D and expanded canvas; CP1 pp. 8-16; CR-03 to CR-08.

pages.title: Care Delivery
pages.subtitle: The people whose trust, time and contributions make the care record useful.
pages.label: 11 DRAFT PERSONAS / GROUP 1 OF 3

items.name: Jess Tran
items.need: Record care once, see the whole picture and connect local and specialist input.
items.friction: Administrative effort, fragmented evidence and disconnected advice.
items.design: Clear episode context, interpretable progress and safe handover. Full care planning and medication/event workflows remain candidate scope.

items.name: Kai
items.need: Be heard, understand progress and take part in care decisions.
items.friction: Retelling the story, unclear visibility and unsuitable digital contexts.
items.design: Plain explanations, eligible contribution and suitable support. Personal progress views and launch phasing need an explicit decision.

items.name: Deb
items.need: Give useful context and understand how to support the person.
items.friction: Feeling excluded or overloaded; uncertainty about involvement.
items.design: Separate tasks and clear visibility. Family relationship is not guardian authority or automatic access to Kai's answers.

blocks.title: Research must reflect real contexts
blocks.body: Co-design with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and diverse lived experiences. Test shared devices, assistance and accessibility; do not assume every person is digitally confident.

decision.title: EXECUTIVE IMPLICATION
decision.text: Protect informed participation and clinician time together. Validate the Engagement Team and specialist contexts separately; do not treat one persona as the whole service.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 03; CMDCS Persona Draft v2 (CP1), pp. 4-6. All profiles are hypotheses, not interview findings.

pages.title: Service Improvement
pages.subtitle: The people who turn data capture into service quality, operational understanding and shared learning.
pages.label: 11 DRAFT PERSONAS / GROUP 2 OF 3

items.name: Rachel Nguyen
items.need: Understand caseload, workforce, performance and model fidelity.
items.friction: Manual reporting, inconsistent data and change pressure.
items.design: Scoped oversight and action ownership. Operations and clinical leadership may need different access.

items.name: Tom Fletcher
items.need: Support accurate registration and close completeness gaps.
items.friction: Chasing staff and maintaining parallel quality workflows.
items.design: Embedded checks, clear owners and verified-source correction; otherwise request clinician input.

items.name: Ananya Rao
items.need: Maintain comparable records, definitions and governed outputs across sites.
items.friction: Mapping complexity, inconsistent records and manual extracts.
items.design: Centre-supported resolution and traceable definitions/releases. Reporting contracts and broader grants need approval.

items.name: Dr Sam Okafor
items.need: Understand implementation and turn fidelity evidence into practical support.
items.friction: Late or context-free evidence and weak feedback to services.
items.design: Connect site context, findings and improvement actions. Person-level access is not automatically granted.

decision.title: EXECUTIVE IMPLICATION
decision.text: Confirm who owns each quality and improvement action. Treat wider dashboards, fidelity and reporting as candidate scope with explicit definitions and access controls.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 03; CP1 pp. 8-11. Source roles and pain points remain unvalidated hypotheses.

pages.title: System Evidence
pages.subtitle: The people who use governed evidence beyond day-to-day care. They do not automatically need the care interface.
pages.label: 11 DRAFT PERSONAS / GROUP 3 OF 3

items.name: Priya Sharma
items.need: Evaluate and commission services using fair comparisons.
items.design: Approved aggregate products with cohort, denominator, quality and comparison limits.

items.name: David Thompson
items.need: Understand accountability, governance and system value.
items.design: Evidence linked to definitions, owners and exceptions. The draft's stewardship claims need confirmation.

items.name: Maya Brooks
items.need: Support consistent national exchange, alignment and approved linkage.
items.design: Agreed schemas, mappings and release manifests; a governed output may be enough without a portal.

items.name: Dr Helen Marsh
items.need: Use approved, appropriately authorised data and return findings to care.
items.friction: Unclear access processes and weak care/research integration.
items.design: Study-specific request, approval, release and closure. Future trial operations are not assumed.

decision.title: ACCESS IS A DECISION, NOT A PERSONA TRAIT
decision.text: Approve purpose, minimum data, recipients and responsibilities first. Guardian, tablet-facilitator and administrator roles remain supporting capabilities, not extra source personas.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 03; CP1 pp. 13-16; D-23/D-24. No legal ownership, access or research authority is established here.

pages.title: From first contact to a clear next step.
pages.subtitle: A care episode holds the whole period of engagement. An individual response is only one contribution within it.
pages.label: THE CARE JOURNEY

items: Intake and triage
Every new patient completes intake; record triage outcome and owner before assessment.
Explain participation
Check purpose, authority, visibility and suitable contact.
Plan the assessment
Use the proposed shared core and clinically eligible modules.
Choose respondent and mode
Confirm who answers, who records, assistance and channel eligibility.
Complete and submit
Save truthfully; confirm the accepted response for this assignment.
Review the evidence
Keep missing work visible; add further eligible modules if needed.
Decide and hand over
Track referral sending, receipt, acceptance/decline and handover; keep follow-up owned.
Continue care and review
Create distinct repeat collections inside the same episode.
Close or transition
Record next care action and reconcile pending requests and reminders.

blocks.title: The journey includes loops and exits
blocks.body: More evidence returns to steps 2-5. A pause or incomplete exit records reason, owner and next action. Only continuing care enters recurring collection; one refusal does not automatically close care.

decision.title: WHAT LEADERSHIP MUST VALIDATE
decision.text: Mandatory new-patient intake is confirmed (D-25). Finalise intake fields/triage and external handover rules (D-26/D-27). Repeated reviews stay in the same episode.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 04, J-01 to J-09; U1/D-25 confirms intake. Clinical/service detail remains D-26/D-27.

pages.title: Close the learning loop.
pages.subtitle: The CMDCS ambition extends beyond collection: evidence should produce accountable action and return to services.
pages.label: SERVICE IMPROVEMENT AND SYSTEM EVIDENCE

items.title: Service Improvement
steps: Agree readiness, definitions, roles and configuration.
Resolve quality issues with evidence and clear ownership.
Interpret performance using cohort, quality and local context.
Agree an action and follow-up; assess what changed.

items.title: System Evidence
steps: Specify purpose, product, recipient and authority.
Validate data, permissions, disclosure and release conditions.
Use only the approved report, exchange or study release.
Assign service or governance action; close use under policy.

blocks.text: A report is not the end of the journey. The next action, owner and feedback to care must be visible.

blocks.title: Across the lifecycle
blocks.body: Support, permission changes, corrections and handover apply whenever needed. Services and satisfaction are conditional. Wider care plans and personal progress remain candidate capabilities.

decision.title: APPROVE THE HANDOFFS
decision.text: For each wider data product, confirm who requests it, who approves release, who acts on the finding and how learning returns. Do not grant care-record access simply to close a reporting loop.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 04, SJ-01 to SJ-08; CP1; CR-01 to CR-08. Wider workflows require D-22 to D-24.

pages.title: Six commitments behind the specification.
pages.subtitle: An executive view of 46 detailed requirements. This summary does not replace their wording or acceptance tests.
pages.label: THE PROPOSED BASELINE

items.title: Use the right record
items.body: Every new patient completes intake before core assessment. Registration is not intake completion or admission. Reviews stay in the relevant episode.

items.title: Choose eligible modes
items.body: Reuse approved instrument versions across permitted respondent, assistance and delivery modes. Not every measure permits self-report.

items.title: Check each purpose
items.body: Separate relationship, authority, permission and answer visibility. Do not make care depend on unrelated research agreement.

items.title: Preserve what happened
items.body: Pin the version presented. Keep source, dates and corrections traceable. Preserve valid zero; do not score missing or invalid codes.

items.title: Leave a next action
items.body: Own intake waits and referral follow-up. Track sending, receipt and receiving decisions separately; reconcile pending work at closure.

items.title: Make outcomes clear
items.body: Accessible mobile/tablet/staff use; safe reset; truthful saving and submission; recovery without duplicate fulfilment.

blocks.title: Scope stays explicit
blocks.body: Mandatory new-patient intake is confirmed (D-25). Operational details remain proposed. Satisfaction, services and the eight CR capabilities need separate scope decisions.

decision.title: APPROVAL STANDARD
decision.text: Approve clinical content, permissions, operational rules and in-scope tests before enabling production workflows. A working prototype is not proof of security, persistence, scoring or delivery.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 05: FR-01 to FR-46, L-01 to L-29 and AC-01 to AC-29; U1/D-25.

pages.title: One status cannot tell the whole story.
pages.subtitle: The interface must distinguish requested work, access, responses and clinical decisions.
pages.label: LOGIC THAT PREVENTS MISUNDERSTANDING

items.title: Assignment
items.body: The requested work is still outstanding.

items.title: SMS link
items.body: This access route is no longer usable.

items.title: Response
items.body: A draft may still exist under policy.

blocks.note: All three can be true together. Next action: use the approved reissue/resume pathway; preserve history and prevent duplicate fulfilment.

rows: Sent / submitted / reviewed
Delivery, accepted response and clinical review are different events.
Assessment / admission / referral
Completion, clinical disposition and onward referral are separate decisions.
Correction / new collection
Correcting a submitted record does not restart ordinary reminders.
Missing / invalid / not applicable
Legacy 998 is invalid/out-of-standard data, not not applicable. Preserve source meaning.

blocks.title: Policy-dependent, not hard-coded assumptions
blocks.body: Guardian pathways, withdrawal/retention, review cadence, episode boundaries and draft/concurrent-attempt handling remain open decisions. No new age rule, reminder interval or scoring threshold is invented here.

decision.title: TEST THE EDGE CASES
decision.text: Require evidence for partial assessments, expired links, uncertain saves, competing submissions, corrections, scope restrictions and closure failures - not just a successful form submission.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 05, status model and acceptance catalogue; D-04 to D-14/D-18. Codebook CB1 mapping.

pages.title: Optimise for understanding, not just speed.
pages.subtitle: Reduce avoidable effort while keeping participation informed, records trustworthy and the next action clear.
pages.label: EXPERIENCE PRIORITIES

items.title: 1. Safe participation
items.body: Correct context, suitable access, clear visibility and support.

items.title: 2. Complete operations
items.body: Review, exits, correction, ownership and handover.

items.title: 3. Useful continuity
items.body: Approved follow-up, interpretable history and learning.

blocks.note: This orders design risk; it does not remove proposed baseline requirements or silently defer candidate scope.

items.title: Name the actual action
items.body: Use distinct language for save, submit, review, disposition and closure. Explain why extra work is requested.

items.title: Show the real state
items.body: Visible source, version, owner and save outcome. No false confirmation or unsupported score comparison.

items.title: Design for real contexts
items.body: Mobile, shared devices, assistance, accessibility and culturally safe co-design. Avoid a digital-native default.

items.title: Support interruption
items.body: Clear blockers and next steps, safe tablet reset and approved resume. Do not promise persistence the system cannot deliver.

decision.title: QUALITY BAR
decision.text: A shorter flow is not better if it hides permissions, loses source context or makes incomplete work appear finished. Validate understanding and task accuracy together.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 06, principles, priorities, content and accessibility; FR-41 proposes WCAG 2.2 AA as a target.

pages.title: Validate, then commit.
pages.subtitle: Progress through evidence gates rather than treating visual polish as launch readiness.
pages.label: DELIVERY AND MEASUREMENT

items: Align
Confirm scope, core journey, persona assumptions and accountable decision owners.
Structure
Test labels, record relationships, navigation and high-risk rules.
Prototype
Exercise clinician, SMS/tablet, family, recovery and operational handoffs.
Specify and implement
Replace sample policy with approved content/rules; build traceable tests.
Verify release
Test real access, persistence, delivery, accessibility and operational support.

rows: Participation and understanding
Baseline/follow-up fulfilment, teach-back and assistance; distinguish permitted skips, pauses and declines.
Effort and continuity
Comparable staff task time, intake-to-core completion and owned next actions; report open/incomplete work.
Integrity and recovery
Complete correction audit and recovery without loss, false success, duplicate fulfilment or access leakage.

blocks.title: No invented targets or timeline
blocks.body: Set denominators, periods, missingness handling and measured baselines before targets. Source pain-point percentages/delays are unverified. No delivery dates, costs or improvement claims are committed.

decision.title: FUND THE VALIDATION WORK
decision.text: Nominate clinical, participant-research, operational, privacy/security and data owners. Resolve the phase conflict and required policies before production; test the wider evidence roles if their capabilities are adopted.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 06, research, delivery sequence, M-01 to M-08 and quality gates.

pages.title: From intake to next care.
pages.subtitle: Clinical team | Boxes = actions; diamonds = decisions.
pages.label: FLOW 1 / THE CARE PATHWAY

nodes.title: New patient: complete intake
nodes.body: Register, check information and record triage.

nodes.title: Wait or exit
nodes.body: Keep owner, reason and next review. Resume intake or track the referral.

nodes.title: Plan the assessment
nodes.body: Assign core + eligible additional measures.

nodes.title: Collect the assigned responses
nodes.body: Use an eligible channel - see Flow 2.

nodes.title: Review evidence + unfinished work
nodes.body: Check completion criteria separately.

nodes.title: More evidence needed
nodes.body: Identify missing evidence; add eligible measures.

nodes.title: Record the clinical decision
nodes.body: Record admission, referral and handover.

nodes.title: Continue care
nodes.body: Plan the next review in the same episode.

nodes.title: Agree the next care action
nodes.body: Close the episode only if appropriate.

decision.title: MANDATORY INTAKE AND NEXT STEPS
decision.text: Every new patient goes through intake (D-25); registration is not completion. Waiting and non-proceeding intakes retain an owner and next action. Clinical admission remains separate.

pages.basis: F-01/F-02/F-05/F-08/F-09/F-17; U1/D-25. Intake detail D-26/D-27 remains proposed.

pages.title: Three channels. One response.
pages.subtitle: Staff set up the task; the eligible respondent or clinician completes it.
pages.label: FLOW 2 / COLLECTION AND CONFIRMATION

nodes.title: Confirm the assignment
nodes.body: Person, version, respondent, support and owner.

nodes.title: Resolve the blocker
nodes.body: Name the owner and next action; then return to setup.

nodes.title: Clinician entry
nodes.body: Record a clinician rating or transcribed answers; retain who supplied them.

nodes.title: SMS link
nodes.body: Send an expiring, account-free link. Check recipient; explain purpose and visibility.

nodes.title: Clinic tablet
nodes.body: Start an isolated session. Explain purpose, visibility and permitted assistance.

nodes.title: Answer, then submit
nodes.body: Use pinned item rules; re-check current permission when submitting.

nodes.title: Check the outcome
nodes.body: Return to this decision. Retry only when safe; never create a duplicate.

nodes.title: This assignment is fulfilled
nodes.body: Clinical review is a separate step.

nodes.title: Tablet only
nodes.body: End and reset; staff re-authenticate to return.

decision.title: PARTICIPATION AND INTERRUPTION
decision.text: Family contribution does not grant guardian authority or access to another person's answers. A draft is not submitted. Tablet cancel/timeout clears local context under approved policy.

pages.basis: F-02/F-03/F-04/F-10. Eligibility, recovery and storage policies remain open; phase conflict D-21 remains.

pages.title: Correct, or ask the clinician?
pages.subtitle: Tom, Data Officer | Jess, authorised clinician | Different responsibilities.
pages.label: FLOW 3 / CORRECTING AN EXISTING RESPONSE

nodes.title: Tom opens the issue
nodes.body: Confirm scope, field, revision and source.

nodes.title: Tom prepares a correction
nodes.body: Check authority; record the new value, source and reason.

nodes.title: Tom requests clinician input
nodes.body: Assign Jess an issue with context, evidence reference and next action.

nodes.title: Review and save the change
nodes.body: Check the latest revision. If it changed, review again before saving.

nodes.title: Jess investigates and responds
nodes.body: Any change uses the audited correction route; otherwise record another resolution.

nodes.title: Confirm the correction + audit
nodes.body: Retain prior/new value, source, actor, time and reason.

nodes.title: Record the request outcome
nodes.body: Keep the issue open until the responsible clinician resolves it.

decision.title: CORRECTION IS NOT A NEW SUBMISSION
decision.text: Keep the original response submitted and preserve provenance. Do not reissue an invitation or restart ordinary reminders. Source eligibility, re-scoring and re-review still need D-13 approval.

pages.basis: F-06 / L-20 / AC-05 / AC-18. Cancel leaves the record unchanged. Only authorised actions are permitted.

pages.title: Other workflows at a glance.
pages.subtitle: Supporting processes stay separate from assessment collection.
pages.label: SUPPORTING FLOWS / SCOPE AND GOVERNANCE

items.title: Preview before committing
items.body: Ananya investigates duplicates or misalignment, records required centre support, previews impact and performs only approved recoverable actions. Suspicion is not identity proof.

items.title: Separate intention from success
items.body: Configure approved versions. At closure, reconcile pending work and onward referrals. Failed, unanswered or declined referrals retain a YSCC follow-up owner.

items.title: Request, approve, release, learn
items.body: Reporting, exchange and research specify purpose and minimum scope, obtain approval, validate and release, then return findings and close use. A request is not an access grant.

blocks.title: Collection recovery remains part of the design
blocks.body: Expired or wrong-recipient links lead to safe support, not exposed answers. Reissue preserves attempt history. Tablet reset does not decide server-draft retention. Resolve uncertain saves before treating work as submitted.

decision.title: GOVERNANCE QUESTION
decision.text: Who can act, on what evidence, within which scope, and how is the result verified? Require answers before implementing shortcuts or external data access.

pages.basis: F-07/F-09/F-11 and candidate F-14 to F-16. These summaries do not replace the detailed F-01 to F-17 catalogue.

pages.title: Organise around the work, not the org chart.
pages.subtitle: Staff need a stable place to find people, understand the current episode and take the next authorised action.
pages.label: THE PROPOSED STAFF STRUCTURE

items.title: My work
items.body: Owned intake waits, referral follow-up and due work.

items.title: People
items.body: Register new patients into intake; then select care context.

items.title: Data quality
items.body: Corrections and record resolution.

items.title: Administration
items.body: Approved roles, versions and rules.

items: Overview
Identity, dates, owner, timeline and next action.
Assessment
Core/modules, progress, evidence review and decision.
Measures
Assignments, delivery attempts, responses and trends.
Consent and respondents
Purpose decisions, relationship, authority and visibility.

blocks.title: Intake and contextual destinations
blocks.body: Intake (ST-27) and referral detail (ST-28) open from My work or People. Services/Feedback remain conditional; correction/audit stays with its record.

decision.title: FINDABILITY TEST
decision.text: Can staff find the right episode, distinguish a response from a reviewed assessment, and return to their work without losing context? Test labels and paths before visual sign-off.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 08, ST-00 to ST-28; intake rule U1/D-25. Surfaces are proposed, not implemented routes.

pages.title: Separate spaces. Governed connections.
pages.subtitle: A participant invitation, a clinician workspace and a research output must not share the same access assumptions.
pages.label: PARTICIPANT ACCESS AND THE WIDER HORIZON

items.title: Open request
items.body: Scoped access and approved recipient checks.

items.title: Understand + answer
items.body: Purpose, visibility, support and pinned questions.

items.title: Confirm + exit
items.body: Real receipt, safe recovery and tablet reset.

blocks.note: Participant surfaces expose only permitted tasks. An invitation link is not a credential for an unrestricted progress portal.

items.title: Care plans and personal progress
items.body: Jess's ongoing-care context and Kai's approved progress view. Define clinical content, authentication and sharing; decide phase.

items.title: Centre and implementation workspaces
items.body: Rachel, Sam and Ananya need scoped performance, fidelity, definitions and improvement actions - not automatic clinical drill-down.

items.title: Governed evidence products
items.body: Priya, David, Maya and Helen may need reports, exchange contracts or approved releases rather than daily access to the care interface.

blocks.title: Access must hold everywhere
blocks.body: Apply the same scope rules to search, counts, deep links, audit and outputs. Persona groups do not automatically become menus or permission grants.

decision.title: ARCHITECTURE DECISION
decision.text: Approve capability and data scope first, then decide the appropriate surface or external output. Keep candidate destinations out of launch navigation until adopted.

pages.basis: Detailed brief 08: PT-01 to PT-09 and candidate EX-01 to EX-08; D-12/D-21 to D-24.
